chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever reproaches a believer, Allah will reproach him in the world and the Hereafter.

key_terms.أَنَّبَ: To reproach, criticize, or point out faults of

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of reproaching a believer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the spiritual gravity of 'tanib' (reproach), warning that publicly exposing a believer's fault invites divine rebuke in both the dunya and akhira. This reflects the Shia emphasis on 'satr' (concealing faults) and maintaining communal dignity, distinguishing between constructive correction and humiliating criticism. The dual consequence highlights that divine accountability mirrors human social dynamics, reinforcing the ethical imperative of modesty in interpersonal relations.
